conventions.convention: Links are nonempty, oriented and smooth, with r ≥ 1. The maximal abelian cover is classified by the kernel of abelianization; its Alexander module is absolute integral H₁, with positive-meridian deck transformations acting as the Laurent variables. Full AC is assumed.

Positive normal disks are oriented so the component tangent followed by the disk orientation gives the ambient orientation. Tubes, labels, basings, endpoint collars, parallel paths and accesses are supplied peripheral data.

Source and target are determined by the positive in-plane normal to the oriented over-strand. Compatible accesses give m_t = m_o⁻¹ m_s m_o; independent access changes require the displayed conjugating factors.

Longitude factors occur in traversal order, with exponent +1 for source-to-target and −1 for target-to-source. Closed preferred longitudes use initial-meridian power minus self-writhe; arbitrary parallels and accesses retain their winding and transport corrections.

The chain procedure receives a genuine triangulated exterior and certified positive-meridian edge loops. It checks edge reversal, triangular cocycle sums and meridian evaluations; it does not recognize the geometric input.

Order means the gcd of E_q generators at the fraction-field rank q, up to a signed Laurent monomial. Diagonal specialization applies to chains; it does not assert that H₁ commutes with this nonflat base change.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming AC, for a nonempty oriented smooth link, A_L is absolute integral first homology of the connected cover classified by the kernel of abelianization, as a left Laurent module under the positive-meridian deck action.

Under AC and the specified link and tube data, the compact exterior is a strong deformation retract of the open complement; the restricted maximal abelian cover is connected, and the lifted deformation retraction is deck-equivariant and induces a Laurent-module isomorphism on H₁.

Closed-link exterior H₁ has the ordered positive-meridian basis and each boundary torus has a unique degree-one class with zero self-meridian coordinate. String-link endpoint groups are free of rank r with compatible meridian accesses; endpoint inclusions induce H₁ isomorphisms and H₂ epimorphisms, with exterior H₂ = 0.

Under AC, any finite CW structure on the compact exterior lifts to a finite-rank free Laurent cellular chain complex whose first homology is the absolute multivariable Alexander module with its positive-meridian deck action.
For the specified local crossing chart and compatible accesses, m_t = m_o⁻¹ m_s m_o. Independently changed accesses obey the explicitly displayed conjugation-correction formula.

The traversal-ordered signed over-meridian product represents the specified string-link longitude or closed-link blackboard parallel; multiplying by the initial meridian to minus self-writhe gives the preferred closed longitude. Arbitrary accesses and parallel windings obey the stated transport formulas.

Under AC, A_L is finitely presented, its Fitting ideals are invariant under triangulation and lift choices, and its rank-indexed order is defined up to a signed Laurent monomial. Diagonal coefficient extension gives the total-linking cyclic-cover chain complex, without asserting a corresponding homology base-change isomorphism.

concerns.concern: The title says “The maximal abelian cover retracts to a compact link exterior”. The Statement and proof correctly retract it onto p⁻¹(E_L), the covering of the compact exterior, rather than onto E_L itself. The literal title fails already for the Hopf link: its contractible maximal abelian cover cannot retract onto T² × I. Clarify the title to name the cover over the compact exterior.

seams_checked.note: The link-specific crossing-cover and meridian-conjugacy arguments are supplied locally rather than inferred from a knot-only presentation theorem. Their compatible accesses, positive meridians and radial exterior identification preserve the prerequisite conventions.

Read the exterior and peripheral definitions. Chosen tubes and positive normal-disk meridians are retained; the link-specific zero-self-coordinate longitude existence is proved locally rather than borrowed as a knot-only conclusion.

The longitude lemma uses the stated determinant crossing sign and self-writhe. Its source-to-target exponent agrees with that determinant convention; mixed crossings do not enter the self-meridian correction.

The twisted-chain definition retains AC, chosen compact exteriors and the full positive-meridian abelianization before the explicit color map. The reviewed torsion consumers do not infer twisted torsion or homology base-change identities merely from the untwisted Alexander-module theorem.
